scope: Read-only analysis of the two existing same-host Redis/RustFS/FUSE qualifications. No new execution; this is not a formal C4 migration result.

observed.mount_error: native fsync snapshot failed, fh: 6, ino: 3, error: record decode: object registration exists without its registry binding
observed.failing_syscall: fsync on existing data-renamed after successful r+b open, seek, write and Python stream flush; close also returned EIO
observed.operation: On the second mount, overwrite 23 bytes at offset 19 in the already written file; failure precedes the second-writer new file.
observed.configuration: Both runs used new catalog names, bucket names and workspace IDs. Within each run the two mount configs are identical except for cache_root; the second path is fresh. Both used local Redis DB3; a globally empty DB was not asserted for workspace mode.

source_diagnosis.status: Strong source diagnosis consistent with both raw warnings; neither run captured the actual rejected Redis keys or a patched execution.

chain.finding: The reopened mount acquires a new catalog writer generation but keeps the same persistent workspace head and write domain. It constructs a new overlay whose in-memory ticket counter starts at zero.

An operation ID hashes volume, workspace, inode and local ticket only. The first block write on both mounts uses the same inode and local ticket even though the durable per-inode mutation order advances.

The receipt object ID is derived from that operation ID, but its content and full-hash object key change when the block contents and receipt entries change. The new key lookup misses, while the old domain/object-ID registration exists.
The registration guard rejects the inconsistent identity and the VFS returns EIO. Even bypassing that guard would leave the durable idempotency row keyed by the reused operation ID.

proposed_repair.change: Give newly admitted mutations a restart-safe operation ID: include a unique writer generation in the ID preimage, or use a durable non-repeating allocation. Keep an admitted operation's ID stable across retries and its derivative receipt/slice IDs coherent. Preserve existing registry and mutation rows; do not bypass identity validation.
proposed_repair.regression: Using the same volume, workspace, Redis and RustFS, write and fsync a file on mount 1 and close normally; on a fresh-cache mount 2 verify original bytes, overwrite the same inode with different data as its first mutation, fsync, create/fsync another file and close; a third fresh-cache mount must read both new results and unmodified bytes. Check distinct operation and receipt IDs, immutable old rows, and stable same-operation retry. The existing src/native_base/runtime/io.rs:2386-2424 remount test checks reads only.
proposed_repair.migration_fence: Still unverified. src/cli.rs:1341-1378 acquires a workspace session but constructs WriteOverlay::new without with_writer_lease; src/native_base/write/overlay.rs:338-379,1358-1385 shows that the no-lease guard uses the currently read head. Test actual old writer publication rejection after the new writer acquires the workspace; catalog release and separate API tests alone cannot prove the mount path's data-write fence.
